title: dependency-snapshot-portal-and-release-simulator
creator: Sofia Gomez
description: Overview: Build a Dependency Snapshot Portal and an accompanying Release Simulator (the 'Simulator') that lets PMs, Eng, Design and Security capture a point-in-time graph of cross-team dependencies, run deterministic cutover simulations, and receive prioritized remediation suggestions. The portal stores immutable snapshots for each planned release window; the Simulator runs scenarios (time-shifted rollouts, staggered canaries, feature gate failures, and infra outages) to surface the critical path, slack, and likely rollback windows. Motivation: existing dependency lists live in spreadsheets and Slack threads and are hard to reason about for multi-team releases. This increases late blockers, reduces predictability for Dedicated/Private rollout windows, and raises customer disruption risk. Goal: reduce cross-team release blockers by 40% within two quarters through earlier visibility, continuous simulation, and standardized remediation playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Portal: create and persist a release snapshot capturing tasks, owners, dependencies, estimated lead times, and related risk tags for up to 5 concurrent initiatives
Simulator: run at least three canned scenarios (parallel deploy, staggered deploy, capacity-constrained fallback) and produce a ranked list of top-5 dependency risks with root-cause traces
Integrations: ingest dependency metadata from Linear (read-only), Confluence links, and a minimal GitHub epic mapping; update must be refreshable on demand
UI: PMs and Engineering leads can annotate snapshots with mitigation tickets or canary windows and export a cutover playbook (PDF)
Measurement: dashboard shows baseline blocker rate and projects expected change; instrumentation fires events to analytics for post-mortem correlation
success_metrics: 40% reduction in cross-team blockers at release cutover within two quarters
Time-to-detect a critical dependency issue reduced from median 5 days to <24 hours
>=75% of release snapshots created at least one sprint before the target release date
Adoption: PM/Eng leads from at least 6 product teams run Simulator at least once per release cycle

2025-02-18 Riley Morgan (Eng): Confirmed we can pull Linear issue graph for teams with a service account. Raised concern about rate limits for very large epics; suggested incremental snapshotting partitioned by team.
2025-02-21 Priya Shah (Design): Shared low-fidelity flows. Emphasized need for a compact timeline view to show slack and critical path; provided FigJam link for feedback.
2025-02-27 Ethan Park (Security): Requested that snapshots include masked customer data and an audit trail. Marked security_review_required = true and requested SSO gating for the portal.

2025-02-28 Luca Patel: Decision - MVP will disable live write-backs into Linear; portal exports mitigation tickets as a CSV and a suggested list for manual creation. This avoids permission complexity for Q1 launch.

2025-03-01 Sofia Gomez: Action items for Eng - (1) exporter proof-of-concept to pull Linear graph, (2) simulator prototype that consumes snapshot JSON and runs parallel/staggered scenarios. Due 2025-03-14.

2025-03-03 Riley Morgan: PoC status - exporter returns graph for three teams; hit an intermittent 429 when querying large epics. Mitigation: implement exponential backoff and incremental pagination. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap/pull/578
2025-03-04 Priya Shah: Design review - updated timeline and annotations accepted. One UX ask: add a 'confidence' slider for each dependency estimate so PMs can mark uncertain lead times.
2025-03-04 Luca Patel: Noted risk - infra simulation (GPU capacity shortfalls during dedicated bursts) requires input from Serving Runtime team. Opening ENG-41200 to track infra modeling work.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Linear rate limits / inconsistent metadata. Mitigation: implement snapshotted ingestion with validation rules; fallback to manual CSV upload.
Risk: Teams treat simulator output as authoritative. Mitigation: label outputs as 'probabilistic guidance' and include explicit confidence bands and suggested mitigation playbooks.
Risk: Security/exposure of release plans. Mitigation: SSO-only access, role-based masking, audit logs retained for 1 year per compliance request.
